_doc: Sources with no extract yet, and why. Every reason is a fact about the saved text or about what was read, not a decision to leave the source out: the sources marked owed are to be read from their page images. Sources that have extracts but were read only in part carry an 'owed' note in source_meta.json (shown in SUMMARY.md).

items.NPS-DEV-POLICY: scanned typescript of 5 pages: the text layer is a damaged OCR (common-word share 0.08, the content-stream-order text no better); to be read from the page images; owed
items.NPS-HS-SPANGLER-HENRY: scanned typescript of 10 pages: the text layer is a damaged OCR (common-word share 0.17; both text variants unreadable); to be read from the page images; owed
items.NPS-BRT-ECOLOGY: 15 pages read by keyword search (no 1863 statement found: 'woods' 5, 'fence' 3, none dated to 1863); not extracted; a full read is owed
items.NPS-MON-LOC-1932: location tables of monuments, markers and tablets: the text layer scrambles the columns and gives no dates of erection; no extract (dates of erection come from the Administrative History and the commemoration study); page images owed if the table of locations is wanted
items.NPS-MON-LOC-1993: location tables of monuments, markers and tablets (1993): the text layer scrambles the columns and gives no dates of erection; compiled with a cooperating association (rights note on the entry); no extract
items.NPS-MCMILLAN-HOUSE: scanned typescript of 15 pages, 5 with text: the text layer is a damaged OCR (common-word share 0.22); to be read from the page images; owed
items.NPS-EXTENSION-1940: scanned typescript of 16 pages (1940 borough-extension report with a historical statement): not yet read for extracts; the text layer reads as prose (common-word share 0.32) but was not searched beyond a keyword count (1863 mentioned 4 times); owed
items.NPS-HCSR: 1958 cemetery survey typescript of 53 pages: the text layer is full of letter errors (for example 'Uattonal Iotty3burg'), the content-stream-order text the same; the survey describes the national cemetery of 1958; to be read from the page images; owed
items.NPS-ROCK-CREEK: scanned typescript of 24 pages, 11 with text: not yet read for extracts (woods mentioned 9 times, 1863 12 times); owed
items.NPS-BRYAN-HOUSE: historic structure report of 39 pages, 10 with text: the pages without text are drawings and photographs; not yet read for extracts; owed (39 pages, 10 with text)
items.NPS-CEM-ENCLOSURES: 1978 study of the national cemetery enclosures (199 pages): the text layer is out of order word by word (a scrambled reading of the wide pages); the content is the walls, fences and gates built 1864-1865 and later, which the 2017 cultural landscape report (PDF pp. 57-83) covers in a readable text and which is extracted from there; no extract from this file
items.NPS-SLAUGHTER-PEN: 60 pages typescript (1980s study of the Slaughter Pen): the text layer is a damaged OCR; pages 7 to 9 (the land of Houck and Hanaway, the stone walls of the Rose, Snyder and Slyder farms, the swampy woodlot of the Sherfy farm) were looked at as page images; an OCR of PDF pp. 5-9 is queued behind the machine lock; the extracts from it are owed
items.NPS-CEM-DEDICATION: scanned typescript of 33 pages on the dedication of the national cemetery: the text layer is a damaged OCR (common-word share 0.08); to be read from the page images; owed
items.NPS-SLYDER-GUIDE: teachers' guide of 47 pages that reprints civilians' accounts of 1863 (published texts); two sentences were read ('Fences were all destroyed'); the accounts are better taken from their own publications; no extract
items.NPS-HB9-1962: 1962 edition of the handbook whose 1954 edition is extracted (the narrative is the same); not extracted separately
items.NPS-DESIGN-GUIDE: 1997 design guide of the Borough of Gettysburg for building owners in the historic district (rights note on the entry: not established as a United States government work); one sentence on early fences of town yards was read as a lead; no extract
items.NPS-EISE-HRS: historic resource study and base map 'Eisenhower Farm, 1762-1967' (268 pages, undated in the text layer): the text layer is a damaged OCR (typescript), its farm histories of 1863 (damage claims of the Bollinger, Douglass, Pitzer, Curren and Redding families) are covered by the three Eisenhower reports in readable text; to be read from the page images (PDF pp. 28-54) if the claims are wanted; owed
items.NPSGOV-COMMEM-WORKS: read: NPS policy text on commemorative works (no Gettysburg dates)
items.NPSGOV-CONFED-LINE: read: no statement on the 1863 landscape beyond the line of the Confederate positions
items.NPSGOV-EAST-CAVALRY: read: no statement on the 1863 landscape
items.NPSGOV-FIRST-DAY: read: one modern description (Barlow Knoll surrounded by agricultural fields); not extracted
items.NPSGOV-LRT-REHAB: read: a project page (the 2012 cultural landscape report is extracted)
items.NPSGOV-PLANNING: read: a list of plans and reports (links only)
items.NPSGOV-TOWN: read: no statement on the 1863 landscape
items.NPSGOV-US-MONUMENTS: read: a list of the United States monuments by state (no dates of erection)
